hero.titleB: Everything a plugin can do, on one screen.
hero.body: This plugin is the official starting point: clone it, rename it and ship a native library with its own menu, screens, locales and a live conversation with the POM.
hero.contextLabel: What the POM told this plugin
steps.label: How to build
steps.title: From a clone to your menu in five steps
steps.one.title: Clone and rename
steps.one.body: Change the package name, the plugin_code and the exported entry point pom_<plugin_code>_plugin_v1.
steps.two.title: Declare the interface
steps.two.body: The pom-plugin-ui/v1 manifest lists menus, submenus, routes, screens, locales, icon, description and screenshots.
steps.three.title: Write the screens
steps.three.body: React components use the React, theme and locale of the POM itself through the host SDK. No second copy of React is bundled.
steps.four.title: Implement the backend
steps.four.body: A versioned C boundary answers query operations: host.configure, host.event, ui.manifest, ui.asset and ui.upstream for a loopback server behind the POM proxy.
steps.five.title: Publish a release
steps.five.body: Package each platform and attach pom-plugin-<os>-<arch>.json to a GitHub release. In Plugins, Add from GitHub installs it.
features.label: Features
features.title: What a plugin can do
features.menu.title: Menus and submenus
features.menu.body: An item with children becomes a sidebar section. This plugin has two: Plugin and Projects.
features.screens.title: Screens and SDK
features.screens.body: Full-screen or centred screens, the POM design kit, React Query and the node API, all from __POM_HOST__.
features.locales.title: Locales
features.locales.body: Each plugin brings its own en and pt-BR catalogs. Keys are namespaced by plugin_code at build time.
features.workspace.title: Shared workspace
features.workspace.body: host.configure delivers workspace_root. Projects lists its folders through the plugin proxy.
features.preferences.title: Preferences
features.preferences.body: A typed schema in the release manifest. The gear on the Plugins card edits it and the backend receives preferences.changed.
features.events.title: POM events
features.events.body: locale.changed, theme.changed, preferences.changed, deployment.started, model.serving and model.stopped, in one pom-plugin-events/v1 envelope for the SDK, the DOM, iframes and the native backend.
features.notifications.title: Notifications
features.notifications.body: A notice for this user, a notice for every node of the network, or an Accept or Reject question in the POM notification bell, answered right here.
features.store.title: Description and screenshots
features.store.body: The manifest description and screenshots show up on the Plugins screen, loaded straight from GitHub.
demo.label: Try it
demo.title: Talk to the POM from this screen
demo.body: Every button below sends a pom-plugin-events/v1 command. A confirmation waits in the POM notification bell (or in a dialog) and the answer comes back as a notification.response event, shown in the history on the side.
demo.localBody: This notice was shown only in this interface.
demo.networkBody: A notice sent by a plugin to every node of the network.
demo.confirmBody: The plugin asked this question through the POM and will read your answer.
demo.eventsHint: Switch the language or the theme, deploy a model or stop one, and watch the events arrive.
demo.backendHint: The native library records host.event envelopes: saved preferences, deployments started and models that start or stop serving.
demo.backendUnavailable: The plugin backend is not reachable right now.
demo.backendEmpty: The backend has not received events yet.
code.label: Code
code.title: The whole contract in a few lines
projects.body: The POM provides this workspace. POM - Plugins reads only its immediate project directories.
projects.unavailable: The shared workspace is not available right now.
projects.empty: No projects were found in the shared workspace yet.
features.loader.title: Loader and installer
features.loader.body: Installing a runtime or starting a process? Keep POM's loader over the screen with loader.show, loader.progress, loader.error and loader.success; Try again comes back as loader.retry.
demo.loaderFailed: A simulated failure. Try again runs the install once more, to the end.
